title: SwasthyaSetu: care without gaps
text: Swasthya Setu helps district coordinators see a medicine shortage before it interrupts community care. This original prototype was built for Track Three of Code for Communities two point zero. We focus on one complete decision workflow: see Primary Health Centre resources, forecast demand, find a safe donor, approve a transfer, and reconcile the stock. Everything shown here uses clearly labelled synthetic records. This walkthrough draft still needs a live Google Gemini generation before final submission.

title: Step 1: inspect the PHC network
text: The health centres workspace connects twelve sample facilities across Odisha, Andhra Pradesh and West Bengal. Each row includes ORS sachet stock, conservative days of cover, free beds and staff attendance. That brings the resource visibility requested by the challenge into one screen. At baseline, five centres have less than seven days of medicine cover, while nearby centres have a surplus. These are realistic demonstration values, not official government stock records, and no patient information is collected.

title: Step 2: update a local snapshot
text: The coordinator can select a centre and update stock, occupied beds and staff present. Input checks reject negative values and numbers beyond the centre's capacity. Saving the snapshot recalculates coverage and transfer recommendations. The demonstration stores changes locally in this browser, so reloading preserves the updated state. Export produces a versioned JSON snapshot for future interoperability. In a real district pilot, authenticated facility reporting and a synchronized backend would replace this browser-local storage.

title: Step 3: inspect the demand forecast
text: The forecast uses the last twenty-eight daily consumption reports to fit a transparent demand trend, then predicts fourteen days ahead. Planning demand adds a conservative buffer based on residual forecast error. Available stock divided by planning demand gives days of cover. This is an inspectable planning heuristic, not a calibrated clinical confidence interval. The graph separates observed consumption from future estimates. Coordinators can understand the numbers behind a warning instead of relying on an unexplained red badge.

title: Step 4: stress-test outbreak demand
text: The outbreak slider changes the demand multiplier and recalculates every warning and feasible transfer. This tests whether the network can still support vulnerable facilities as demand rises. Some needs may remain unresolved when donors cannot safely release stock. The system then requires escalation rather than proposing an unsafe transfer. This screenshot was captured after increasing demand in the same browser session following an approved transfer, so its totals reflect both the changed inventory and the stress scenario.

title: Step 5: review a safe redistribution plan
text: At the initial baseline, the engine proposes five routes moving a total of nine hundred and sixty-five ORS sachets. Recipients are ranked by urgency. Donors within the same state are ranked by approximate distance. Every planned allocation protects fourteen days of stock at the donor and targets seven days at the recipient. The first proposed route moves two hundred and twenty-seven sachets from Jagatsinghpur to Pattamundai, across district boundaries. Travel estimates are approximate and require real route verification.

title: Step 6: approve and reconcile the dispatch
text: We approved that first demonstration dispatch in the running application. The donor stock decreased, the recipient stock increased, and the remaining proposed quantity changed from nine hundred and sixty-five to seven hundred and thirty-eight sachets. The ledger records reference Setu zero zero zero one, the source and destination identifiers, the quantity and the approval time. Total stock is conserved. In production, dispatch and confirmed receipt would be separate authorized steps; here, the completed movement is explicitly a simulation.

title: Step 7: inspect shared model intelligence
text: The federated intelligence screen computes separate model statistics for the three state nodes. Each state shares only five sufficient statistics, rather than individual facility consumption histories. Aggregating them reproduces the shared linear regression coefficients exactly. This is an executable federation simulation, with all nodes running in one browser. It does not claim secure aggregation or formal privacy. A production rollout needs independent state services, authenticated updates and governance review before connecting actual health-system records.

title: Step 8: read the validation evidence
text: Forecast evaluation uses a chronological split: twenty-one days for training and the final seven days for testing. Across eighty-four held-out observations, the synthetic fixture produces seven point nine percent weighted absolute percentage error and a mean absolute error of two point eight sachets. These figures are not claims of real-world accuracy. Six passing engine tests check stock conservation, donor protection, rejection of unsafe approvals, exact federation, known-trend forecasting and holdout evaluation. A pilot must measure actual stockout days and alert precision.

title: Step 9: connect meaningful Google AI
text: The Google Gemini integration sends computed evidence to an operations briefing assistant. It explains urgent shortages, feasible transfers, unresolved needs and checks before approval in English, Hindi, Odia, Telugu or Bengali. Gemini cannot alter inventory or approve dispatches. On GitHub Pages, a restricted key is held only in memory and sent directly to Google's API. Vercel also supports a server-side key. No valid key was available during this recording, so a live generated briefing must be added before submission.

title: Pilot path: one district, then state networks
text: Swasthya Setu is publicly deployed on GitHub Pages, with original source code, reproducible tests and a twelve-slide deck. The next step is one district in shadow mode using consented historical consumption data. Compare stockout days, alert precision and donor reserve violations against a warehouse-only baseline. Then add batch expiry checks, authenticated approvals, dispatch receipts and independent state nodes. The opportunity is practical coordination: moving existing supplies to the community that needs them, without creating another shortage elsewhere.
